findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/clouds-ground-cumulus.png; same folder: clouds-static-animated.png, clouds-quality-0.7-ground.png, clouds-ground-cumulus-into-sun.png, perf-ground-cumulus-overhead-1440p.png, transparent-quads-broken-layer.png, perf-pad-1440p.png (x 200-1000, y 300-750 native), clouds-ascent-2kms-1800m-moving.png, clouds-ascent-2kms-1800m-converged.png
findings.defect: The 'fair-weather cumulus at noon' view from the pad is a ceiling of huge smooth grey lumps: putty or a smoke simulation, not cumulus. Overhead bodies span half the frame, their undersides are stretched into fluted 'pulled taffy' streaks (upper left), edges are out of focus, and nothing is finer than a few hundred metres. The gaps between the clouds are neutral grey (149,149,151 at (520,300); 152,151,152 at (1050,200)) because a translucent sheet lies over the field: at a nominal cover of 0.4 only 2 % of the sky pixels are blue (B-R > 18) in clouds-ground-cumulus.png, clouds-static-animated.png and perf-ground-cumulus-overhead-1440p.png. Seen from below against clear sky (transparent-quads-broken-layer.png) a cumulus is one uniform grey blob with a blurred outline. Flying past clouds at 1.8 km the frame is blur with nothing to focus on. At native 1440p in animated mode (perf-pad-1440p.png) the clouds are airbrushed against razor-sharp terrain, with a featureless white fan that ends in a soft arc across the blue sky.
findings.realReference: Launch-pad and airfield photographs under fair-weather cumulus: separate clouds 0.3-1.5 km across with flat grey bases all at one height, brilliant white cauliflower tops whose curled edges are sharp down to the pixel, ragged wisps at the fringes, saturated blue between them, ranks of clouds foreshortened toward the horizon. Cover 0.4 means more blue than white overhead. Next to a cumulus you see turbulent knots and filaments metres across.
findings.likelyCause: Shape: cloudDensityAt in src/render/atmosphere/shaders/clouds.ts (about l.181-227) thresholds ONE Perlin-Worley lookup of a 128^3 texture tiled over baseNoiseScaleM = 9000 m (texel 70 m, dominant features about 2.2 km; the Perlin octaves halve in amplitude, so 140 m detail carries about 3 % of the signal) times a height gradient. The layer is 1.9 km thick, so shapes are near-vertical extrusions of 2 km blobs, and windShear 0.6 (cloudWind, l.169) shears the lookup about 1.1 km over the layer depth: the fluted undersides. Edge: lowEdgeSoftness 0.12 plus erosion that only displaces the surface by at most detailErosion 0.24 using a 32^3 detail texture (texel 34 m): no crisp edge, no holes. Buffer: half resolution, one ray per 2 x 2 block per frame, bilinear upsample. Veil: cloudColumnAt l.131 gives every column with coverage above highCoverageStart 0.22 a stratiform sheet under the map's cloud top, even when that top (3 km in this scene) is at cumulus height. Cover: threshold lowered by half the erosion depth (l.196) and mesoscale swing mesoscaleAmplitude 0.8 x 4 c (1 - c) (l.125). Tunables in data/defs/render/earth.clouds.json.
findings.fixDirection: Rebuild the low-cloud shape the way shipped renderers that pass this test do (Schneider / Horizon, Hillaire / Frostbite): cumulus-scale base noise (tile 3-4 km, vertical frequency at least the horizontal one), density = remap(base, 1 - coverage, 1, 0, 1) x a per-type height profile, then erosion by three octaves of high-frequency Worley fBm weighted to the edges and deep enough to open holes, curl-noise distortion of the detail lookup, edge softness an order of magnitude smaller, wind shear at most 0.15. No sheet where the map's cloud top lies within about 1.5 km of the low layer's top (give that coverage to the cumulus); where a sheet exists make it white and fibrous, not a grey film. Assert that the sky fraction seen from the ground equals the map's cover. Keep the detail through the resolve: edge-aware (alpha/depth-guided) upsample or full-resolution march near the camera. Iterate at native 1440p, animated, beside pad photographs.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/leo-day.png; same folder: leo-day-limb.png (x 0-420, y 380-600), sampling-low-orbit-limb.png, sampling-low-orbit-limb-animated.png, clouds-quality-0.7-orbit.png, perf-low-orbit-1440p.png (x 1300-1940, y 800-1160 native)
findings.defect: From 400 km the cloud layer is a blurred field of same-sized round blobs (bubble wrap: 10-15 px, about 7-10 km each at 720p) and soft white smears. No cloud casts a shadow on the sea at a sun elevation of 50 deg, no cloud has a lit and a shaded side or any relief, the brightness is one flat light grey (about 200,200,200), there is no thin cirrus, no cloud street, no texture below the blob size. Toward the limb the bands break into 2-4 px blocks and a woven stipple. Everything in the layer is softer than the planet's own edge: it reads as a low-resolution procedural overlay. The 1440p animated frame shows the same blobs, only larger.
findings.realReference: ISS day-side photographs at the same obliquity: cloud detail to the pixel; popcorn cumulus of every size down to sub-pixel sparkle, organised in streets and open or closed cells; each cloud with a crisp dark shadow displaced on the sea; towers and anvils with bright sunward flanks, grey lee sides and long shadows on the decks below; translucent cirrus veils; cloud brightness from brilliant white to thin grey.
findings.likelyCause: (a) Pattern: at orbit footprints (0.4-0.7 km) the shape noise is past its useful mips (cloudNoiseKeep, level about 4.4 of a 9 km tile), so what is seen is cLow modulated by one octave of inverted Worley cells of the mesoscale noise (nMeso = meso.g; mesoscaleScaleM 40 km / 4 cells = 10 km) in cloudColumnAt, shaders/clouds.ts l.110-125: single-scale round cells. (b) Each pixel is a cloud FRACTION lit with the mean light of a column (cloudStackStep): nothing to shade. (c) Shadows: the near shadow map's half extent grows with altitude (src/render/atmosphere/clouds.ts l.692: 30 km + 2.5 x altitude, about 1,000 km at 400 km, i.e. 1.95 km per texel, band-limited further by shadowFilter), coarser than the 1-4 km shadow offsets; beyond it the far term is a blurred coverage lookup. (d) Half-resolution quarter-area march, bilinear upsample, cloud geometry read by nearest textureLoad (shaders/march.ts l.186): the blocks near the limb.
findings.fixDirection: Give the orbit regime its own detail and its own shadow. Detail: a multi-octave, anisotropic mesoscale field (streets along the wind, cells from 50 km down to the pixel), or photo-derived tiling cloud-texture sets per cloud type (the terrain package already builds materials from photo sources), driving fraction AND optical depth. Relief: a cloud-top height from that field, shaded by the sun through its gradient where shapes are unresolved. Shadows: per pixel, evaluate the same column density at the point displaced along the sun direction (parallax shadow on the surface and on lower cloud) instead of a 2 km shadow map. Resolution: march this regime at full resolution (few steps per ray up there) or upsample edge-aware with geometry filtered like colour. Compare with ISS frames at 1440p.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/clouds-ground-sunset.png (clouds x 440-840, y 340-440; ground x 700-1280, y 465-540); same folder: leo-low-sun.png (x 380-620, y 600-720), perf-low-orbit-terminator-1440p.png (x 900-1300, y 1180-1440 native, animated)
findings.defect: With the sun 3 deg up, the clouds in front of the sun are cut by dark zig-zag triangles and wedge-shaped shafts fanning out from the sun (saw teeth 20-40 px wide, visible without zooming), and the ground carries knife-straight light and shadow stripes. From orbit with the sun 4 deg up the same fault shows as a comb of 1-2 px streaks parallel to the sun's azimuth hanging from the edge of every cloud across cloud and sea; it is in the native 1440p animated frame too, so temporal accumulation does not hide it.
findings.realReference: Sunset under broken cumulus: soft crepuscular rays whose edges are penumbrae that widen with distance, clouds shading each other in smooth gradients. From orbit at low sun: long, soft-edged, tapering shadows of cloud towers on decks and sea; never parallel hairlines or saw teeth.
findings.likelyCause: cloudShadowFsWgsl in src/render/atmosphere/shaders/clouds.ts (l.913-984): every shadow-map texel marches the whole 11.3 km layer along the projection line in shadowSteps = 16 equal steps. At the 4 deg clamp (SHADOW_MIN_ELEVATION, src/render/atmosphere/clouds.ts l.51 and l.717) that line is about 160 km long, one step about 10 km, so sFront (channel g: where the cloud begins) is quantised to 10 km and neighbouring texels land on different quanta. The lookups tau = clamp((g - s) b, 0, r) in atmoCloudShadowAt (shaders/march.ts l.38-39) and in the core's cloudShadow (src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts) then interpolate front distance, extinction and optical depth of unlike texels bilinearly: triangles and streaks along the sun direction. Below 4 deg the map's direction is not the sun's at all.
findings.fixDirection: Either make the map adequate at low sun or stop using it there. Map: step count proportional to the path length through the occupied altitude range, stratified and jittered per texel; store filterable quantities (transmittance at a few fixed depths, i.e. a small deep/opacity shadow map, or moments) instead of front + mean extinction, and pre-filter it; never interpolate g across a cloud edge. Low sun (under about 8 deg): blend to ray-marched samples along the TRUE sun direction (a longer cone of 8-12 blue-noise samples, accumulated) for clouds and shafts, and for the ground use the coverage term with a penumbra that grows with distance. Add a sunset close-up to the specs with a bound on high-frequency energy along the sun direction.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/clouds-under-deck.png; same folder: clouds-shadow-under-deck.png, shadow-lit-quad-under-the-deck.png, clouds-ground-cumulus.png (mountains y 440-490; ground band y 495-530), perf-ground-cumulus-overhead-1440p.png, ascent-10km.png and sampling-ascent-5km-horizon-animated.png (shadows on the islands)
findings.defect: Everything in cloud shadow is saturated navy and far too dark. Under the overcast deck the sea is (15,23,39) and the islands (55,66,87) below a deck of (120,117,117); the lit test surface under the deck is at 0.002 of its clear-sky value (hand-off section 5) and clouds-shadow-under-deck.png is a near-black frame at daylight exposure. Cumulus shadows on the mountains are (41,51,70) against (138,129,123) in sun: 6.7 : 1 in luminance with the hue flipped from beige to navy; the shadowed ground is a blue-black band (11,17,27). From 5-10 km the cloud shadows on the pink islands read as lakes.
findings.realReference: Under a thick overcast the ground receives 10-25 % of the clear-sky illuminance as WHITE diffuse light: a grey scene with no blue cast, terrain luminance about albedo x deck luminance. Shadows of cumulus are 3-5 times darker than sunlit ground and only slightly cooler, because sky and the bright clouds around fill them.
findings.likelyCause: The package publishes only an optical depth ('clouds.shadowMap', farShadowOpticalDepth) and a clear-sky 'atmosphere.skyIrradianceLut'. The deferred lighting (src/render/core/lighting/deferred.ts l.206 'sunE *= cloudShadow(...)', l.234-236 ambient from the clear-sky table; chunk cloud_shadow in src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts) applies pure Beer-Lambert exp(-tau / muS) to the sun and adds the unshadowed BLUE clear-sky irradiance. The light a cloud transmits diffusely (two-stream: roughly 1 / (1 + 0.1 tau) of the sun under a deck) and the light of the cloud base and sides are missing. The clouds themselves are lit with exactly that two-stream term (cloudMarchFsWgsl l.722-731), so cloud and ground disagree.
findings.fixDirection: Carry a diffuse term with the shadow: E_ground = E_sun mu [exp(-tau/mu) + (T_diffuse(tau) - exp(-tau/mu))], the second part white, with T_diffuse from the same two-stream constants as the cloud lighting; and replace the sky irradiance under cloud by a cover-weighted mix (1 - f) E_clear_sky + f E_cloud_base (grey-white). The core's cloud_shadow chunk has to return (direct, diffuse): file the request to core-support with the formula and the map channel that carries it. Extend shadows.spec.ts: under the deck 0.1-0.3 of the clear value and a neutral hue (B/R within 25 % of the sunlit one).

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/tunables-shipped.png; same folder: clouds-deck-top.png, clouds-above-deck.png, perf-above-a-deck-1440p.png, shadow-lit-quad-low-orbit.png, shadow-lit-quad-above-the-deck.png (left third), transparent-quad-over-clouds-from-orbit.png, transparent-quad-under-clouds-from-orbit.png, transparent-quad-under-deck.png (x 850-1000, y 560-640), clouds-under-deck.png (x 700-1200, y 180-360)
findings.defect: An overcast never looks like cloud from any side. From just above (4-6 km) it is smooth snow dunes with hairline creases and a ruler-straight horizon. From 25 km with the shipped tunables the whole deck is covered with thin squiggly contour lines, like wood grain or a topographic map. Straight down from 400 km (shadow-lit-quad-low-orbit.png) it is mid-grey (about 150,148,145) mottled granite with bright worm-like veins; in the transparent orbit test it is a blank, perfectly uniform grey card (200,198,193). From below the base is a watercolour smear with thin bright vein lines and one hard-edged swoosh; from 6 km straight down the smooth sheet beside the billows shows stepped contour terraces.
findings.realReference: Stratocumulus from an airliner, a U-2 or the ISS: a quilt of closed cells or cotton-ball lumps 0.5-2 km across with rounded tops and soft dark gaps, pebbly texture everywhere, long shadows at low sun; bright white (albedo 0.5-0.7), never mid-grey; the horizon softened by haze. From below: soft mottling of darker and lighter grey, no lines.
findings.likelyCause: Sheet tops are an analytic bell profile with topReliefM 700 m of the 9 km shape noise carved in (cloudDensityAt l.244-255): only low frequencies, hence dunes. The squiggles are iso-lines of the eroded surface: slabs restart at the bisected surface (l.618-644), grazing hits are lit as one 'sliver' slab, and slabs that add little reuse the light of the last lit slab (reuseBelow, l.693-697), so the soft edge is sampled at discrete depths (the code's own comments name 'contour lines'). Veins: thin gaps between col.lowTop and col.highBase (cloudColumnAt l.138) and the (nr - 0.5) x 0.35 x (1 - fade) term at the fade boundary. Grey from orbit: the unresolved deck is lit by the highOrders term at the mean optical depth; nothing ties its brightness to the reflectance of a thick layer.
findings.fixDirection: Give decks a cell structure of their own: a Worley-based closed-cell height field (cells 0.7-2 km, several octaves, domain-warped) for the top, opacity dips between the cells, relief of 150-400 m that both the eye march and the light march resolve. Light continuously: interpolate the light between lit slabs instead of reusing it, dither slab starts with blue noise and accumulate, so no iso-line survives. Make deck brightness follow two-stream reflectance, tau / (tau + about 8), so thick decks are white from above; where cells are unresolved shade by the cell field's gradient. Add assertions: no line-like features (ridge detector) in tunables-shipped, deck reflectance range from 25 km and from 400 km.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/sampling-ascent-5km-horizon.png (bank x 0-450, y 225-400; sea x 440-740, y 540-710); same folder: ascent-10km.png (x 450-1280, y 360-400), sampling-ascent-10km-horizon.png, sampling-ascent-10km-horizon-animated.png, perf-ascent-10-km-1440p.png (x 900-2560, y 730-790 native, animated)
findings.defect: (a) Cloud banks toward the horizon are built from horizontal bars. In the deterministic acceptance frames the far bank is horizontally smeared slabs with abrupt vertical cut-offs and the near bank at 5 km is ruled with lines every 3-6 px; at native 1440p in animated mode the bank is still a stack of thin horizontal lines (venetian blind). (b) In sampling-ascent-5km-horizon.png (deterministic: the mode of every acceptance and mission screenshot) blob-shaped patches of open sea are hatched: alternate pixel rows are 110-112 and 95-97 where the converged animated frame of the same view is a uniform 90 (2.9 % of the frame, 17 % row contrast, identical in two runs). The patches are phantom brightening that exists only with the frozen step phase.
findings.realReference: A distant cumulus or stratocumulus bank seen edge-on: lumpy tops and towers, crisp against the sky, continuous tone inside; never horizontal lamination. Open sea between clouds is one tone.
findings.likelyCause: (a) All rays of a pixel row share an elevation and so a step pattern: xi is frozen at 0.5 when atmo.misc.z = 0 (cloudMarchFsWgsl l.452), and the step count, the coarsen factor (l.479-489) and the discrete reuse of the last lit slab (l.693-697) change in whole steps from row to row: coherent bars; animated mode only dithers them. sampling.spec.ts tests a row period of exactly 2 in the horizon band only. (b) The patches are unresolved thin low cloud in front of the sea while the camera is INSIDE the layer's altitude range (5 km, between 1.2 and 12.5 km): the altitude shortcut for 'behind' in marchFsWgsl (shaders/march.ts l.287-291) does not apply there, the near candidate decides by distance with cloudGeom read by nearest textureLoad while the cloud colour is bilinear (l.184-186), and the composite (compositeFsWgsl l.400-406) gives the nearer pixel row of each 2 x 2 block the near candidate and the farther row the far one.
findings.fixDirection: (a) Keep a deterministic but spatially varying step phase in deterministic mode (fixed blue noise by pixel and frame index) and remove the row coherence at its source: continuous step placement along the ray (no whole-step jump between adjacent elevations), light interpolated between lit slabs. For layers seen edge-on beyond about 80 km integrate the layer per pixel column against a mesoscale top-height field so the bank has lumpy tops. (b) Decide 'behind' from altitudes whenever the surface lies below the layer and the cloud begins nearer than the surface, wherever the camera is; sample cloud radiance and geometry with the same filter; extend sampling.spec.ts to the sea region of the 5 km view and to row periods 2-8.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/ascent-10km.png; same folder: ascent-25km.png, ascent-40km.png, ascent-80km.png, sampling-ascent-5km-horizon-animated.png
findings.defect: Looking down from 5-40 km the cumulus are flat white splats: soft-edged cut-outs of even brightness with no tops, flanks or visible height, like cotton pads or flecks of paint. Large systems are airbrushed white masses without any texture (ascent-25km centre, ascent-10km left third, ascent-80km lower right). Shadows are navy blobs directly underneath the nearest clouds and absent further out. From 80 km the scattered field is a recognisably procedural curdled pattern.
findings.realReference: High-altitude balloon and U-2 footage and booster onboard cameras: cumulus fields as crisp, bright, lumpy heaps with visible height (shaded sides, shadows offset on the sea), granular texture across large systems down to the pixel, streets and cells.
findings.likelyCause: The smooth shape field of the first finding seen from above: the height gradient closes every shape into a soft dome, the erosion fades out by detailFadeFootprintM = 400 m (cloudDensityAt l.193) so nothing breaks the outline at these distances, and beyond mip level 4 the shapes become the uniform 'fraction'. Top lighting is nearly flat because the six cone samples see only the smooth shape and the highOrders and ambient terms dominate. The near shadow map covers 30 km plus 2.5 x altitude with 1024 texels and one density band limit.
findings.fixDirection: With the new shape model keep an intermediate octave (150-600 m) alive up to about 2 km footprints, keep edges sharp, and let the sun shade the tops (relief seen by the light samples, or a top-height gradient where unresolved). Shadows for every cloud in view: a fine and a coarse shadow cascade, or the per-pixel parallax shadow proposed for orbit.

findings.defect: Views drawn through the full-resolution tile march (planet disc under 512 px) are peppered with single dark pixels: navy dots along cloud edges (earth-60000km.png (552,249) = 35,49,135 among neighbours of luma 115-164; (761,420) = 13,10,77) and near-black dots inside bright cloud toward the terminator (earth-60000km-crescent.png (555,351) = 16,12,15 and (543,353) = 25,22,19; small-shell-clouds-fov10.5.png (649,307) = 15,11,9). A strict isolated-pixel test counts 9, 4 and 6; by eye at 3x there are dozens along the edges. They are stable in a still and will crawl as the planet turns. The half-resolution path at 1440p (explore/z-60000-1440p.png) has none.
findings.realReference: DSCOVR and Apollo 17 whole-disc photographs: cloud edges are soft gradients; there is no single-pixel hole anywhere on the disc.
findings.likelyCause: cloudMarchFsWgsl(true) (shaders/clouds.ts l.443-447): one ray per pixel, xi = 0.5, no temporal or spatial filter, and compositeFineFsWgsl copies the texel as it is. A pixel whose 20 km footprint falls into a small gap of the fraction field shows the surface, and the surface there is in full cloud shadow, because the core's far shadow term reads the coverage map at level 0 (cloudShadow in src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts: textureSampleLevel(cloudCoverageMapTex, ..., 0.0), optical depth farShadowOpticalDepth / muS) while the march reads it at max(log2(footprint / texel), 1) plus noise wander: a shadow with no cloud above it.
findings.fixDirection: Filter the tile: 4 rotated-grid rays per pixel (the tile is at most 512 x 512 and the rays are short) or a transmittance-aware 3 x 3 filter before the composite. Read the coverage for a cloud and for its shadow at the same level (pass the footprint level to the far term). Add an isolated-dark-pixel count to smallshell.spec.ts (must be 0, also at the crescent phase).

findings.defect: Earth from the Moon's distance through a 2.5 deg lens (disc about 550 px, over the 512 px tile limit, so the half-resolution path): the sunlit limb is a staircase of 4-6 px blocks instead of a smooth arc, clouds at the limb are square steps, and all cloud on the disc is a blur 6-10 px wide. Two runs of the same commit differ in 5,227 pixels of this frame by more than 12/255.
findings.realReference: Apollo 8 / 17 and Kaguya telephoto frames of Earth: a razor-sharp, perfectly smooth limb with a thin blue haze line; cloud swirls and filaments crisp down to the film grain.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/atmosphere/select.ts l.134-138: the full-resolution path is chosen by pixel size (FINE_TILE_SIZE = 512), not by kilometres per texel. Here a half-resolution texel is 26 km and a checkerboard block 52 km against a 100 km atmosphere and a 12 km cloud layer, so the two-candidate interpolation, the nearest cloud-geometry lookup and the bilinear cloud upsample all work on blocks. The coverage map is never read finer than level 1 (cloudColumnAt l.92) and no noise survives at this footprint: blur. Every zoomed or intermediate-distance view with a disc over 512 px and texels of several km is in this state (the hand-off only says the switch is a cut).
findings.fixDirection: Choose the path by footprint: march at full resolution wherever a half-resolution texel exceeds a fraction (about 1/8) of the shell depth at the limb, with a tile sized to the disc's screen rectangle, or march a stencilled limb band at full resolution and the interior at half; blend the two across the threshold. Allow the map's finest level when the footprint is below its texel.

findings.defect: 1.5 deg after sunset the clouds are still bright tan and shaded as if the sun were up, and the frame has a 2 px dark violet border on its top, left and right edges (row 0: 76,71,85; row 2: 139,116,102; column 0: 64,54,60; column 2: 137,109,83). The border is the true current colour (dim violet-grey cloud); the interior is history left from the previous scene of the spec (sun +3 deg, same camera).
findings.realReference: Five to ten minutes after sunset low cumulus are dark blue-grey silhouettes against the bright twilight sky, at most with pink edges on the highest tops. Cloud lighting never lags behind the sun and never leaves a frame around the picture.
findings.likelyCause: CLOUD_RESOLVE_FS_WGSL in shaders/clouds.ts: history is used only when the reprojected position is more than a texel inside the target (l.845), so border texels never have any; for a pixel that has not moved the neighbourhood clamp is off (l.853-854) and a new march is blended at atmo.misc.w = 0.125 (l.862; set in src/render/atmosphere/clouds.ts l.664) once every four frames. After the 40 frames screens.spec.ts waits, 0.875^10 = 26 % of the far brighter sunset radiance remains. Only exposure changes are compensated (misc.x); a change of sun direction, sun colour or eclipse share is not. In the game this is every sunrise, sunset and eclipse under time warp.
findings.fixDirection: Detect a lighting change between frames (sun direction relative to the body, sun illuminance at the cloud layer, eclipse visibility) and raise the blend weight or re-enable the clamp in proportion; or store radiance divided by a per-frame reference illuminance and multiply it back. Give border texels history clamped to the edge. Make the spec reset history or wait for convergence, and assert that the border rows equal the rows next to them.

findings.defect: Sunset clouds are one hue, khaki to mustard brown, in sun and in shade alike: (112,82,49) at (300,150), (146,110,65) at (1100,250), (133,104,80) near the sun, the 'sky' between them (139,119,102). No orange or red sunlit faces, no blue-grey shaded sides, no blue or turquoise sky above: a sepia filter.
findings.realReference: Sun 3 deg up over broken cumulus: faces toward the sun glow orange-gold, undersides pink-orange, parts in shade are blue-grey to violet (lit by the blue sky overhead), the sky runs from yellow at the horizon through pale green-blue to blue: strong warm against cool.
findings.likelyCause: The sheet of the first finding fills the gaps and is itself sun-reddened, so no blue sky is seen. Shaded cloud gets little blue: the ambient term in cloudMarchFsWgsl (l.729-731) is the hemispherical irradianceLut (near neutral at low sun, it includes the orange horizon) plus a ground bounce, against the isotropic highOrders sun term (diffuseScatter 0.7) that fills shaded parts with reddened sunlight.
findings.fixDirection: Light shaded cloud with the radiance of the sky away from the sun (two or three lookups of the sky-view table, or a zenith-weighted irradiance) instead of the hemispherical mean, cut the isotropic sun term where the optical depth toward the sun is large, and remove the sheet in fair weather. Assert a warm/cool contrast in the spec (sunlit R/B above 2.5, shaded B/R above 1.1).

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/earth-60000km.png; same folder: clouds-orbit-vs-map.png, earth-moon-distance.png, explore/z-60000-1440p.png (final state at native 1440p, animated)
findings.defect: From 60,000 km and beyond the weather is white paint with blurred outlines: two tones (white, sea), no translucent cirrus, no grey thin cloud, no texture inside a system, no sun shading on fronts and cyclone bands. The hand-off lists this as 'white-or-not'; it is what the player sees for the whole of a lunar transfer.
findings.realReference: Apollo 17 Blue Marble and DSCOVR EPIC frames: an enormous tonal range in cloud, from gauzy veils the sea shows through to dense white cores; fibrous cirrus, speckled cumulus fields, sharply drawn comma clouds with shaded structure.
findings.likelyCause: The coverage is turned into cover first and opacity second: cLow = c x lowCoverageGain 0.9, the 'thin' density only below c = 0.6 (cloudColumnAt l.136), a quarter of the baked map at 0.9-1 (hand-off). The opacity mottling (lowDensityVariation) is faded to its mean by mesoKeep and largeKeep at footprints of tens of km (l.115-116), and a transmittance under 0.004 is set to 0 (l.748). The map is read one level above its finest.
findings.fixDirection: Treat the map as optical depth with a wide range (tau from about 0.3 to 60) and its cloud-top channel as type, keep large-scale opacity variance at every footprint (a variance-preserving term instead of a fade to the mean), shade by the cloud-top height gradient, and if the baked map is saturated ask bake-earth for an optical-depth map with real dynamic range.

findings.defect: At qualityScale 0.7 the shaded slopes and creases of the deck are covered with coarse stipple (sandpaper, styrofoam) that the quality 1 frame does not have, and there are 1-2 px dark ticks on the left and right frame edges at y about 395 and 540. The quality governor puts weaker machines at 0.7, so those players see this, shimmering. The spec compares mean luminance only (+2.34 %) and cannot see it.
findings.realReference: Cloud surfaces have no grain at any distance; a lower quality setting may soften them, never texture them.
findings.likelyCause: The step budget is cloudSteps x q^2 (src/render/atmosphere/clouds.ts l.548: 96 to 47) and up to 10 % of the cloud in a pixel reuses the previous slab's light (reuseBelow, shaders/clouds.ts l.501), so single marches are noisy; the resolve averages about eight marches (weight 0.125) with no spatial filter; border texels have no history (l.845).
findings.fixDirection: Lower resolution or far-field steps before near-field light quality; add a small alpha/depth-aware spatial filter of cloud radiance to the resolve when q < 1, or lengthen the accumulation for still pixels. Test with a high-pass energy metric at 0.7 against 1 instead of the mean alone.

findings.defect: The twilight sky is violet-grey, not blue. 40 deg up, 3 deg after sunset: (31,33,58); at 20-30 deg (39,38,63) and (46,43,65), red at or above green; with auto exposure the whole anti-twilight view is lavender (109,110,142 to 134,129,153). At sunset the sky above the glow is slate-mauve (92,99,122). The spec only requires red <= 1.02 x green. The Belt of Venus and the Earth's shadow band themselves are recognisable and good.
findings.realReference: Civil twilight opposite the sun: above the pink belt the sky is clear blue to blue-grey with green well above red (roughly 120,150,190 on a normal exposure), deepening to dark blue overhead; the Earth's shadow is slate blue.
findings.likelyCause: Three bands cannot follow the Chappuis absorption of light that has already been reddened; data/defs/render/earth.atmosphere.json ships ozoneAbsorption (1.9, 1.721, 0) e-6 as a compromise (hand-off section 6) and band-averaged Rayleigh (7.1, 13.8, 32.5) e-6, which lowers blue against red.
findings.fixDirection: Fit the three-band coefficients to a spectral reference at twilight instead of a band average (minimise the chromaticity error of the float64 reference model run spectrally at sun elevations from -6 to +5 deg), or carry a fourth band for the Chappuis window in the tables; assert green/red above 1.3 at 40 deg up.

findings.defect: The lower edge of the night-side limb glow is stair-stepped (1 px steps on runs of about 30 px, an orange fringe drawn as dashes) and the orange layer is a 1-2 px hairline under a uniform periwinkle band (154,173,223). The review named the stair-step; it is still there with clouds on.
findings.realReference: ISS photographs of the limb with the sun just under the horizon: a smooth arc in layers, deep orange-red at the bottom several pixels thick, a thin pale band, then blue fading into black.
findings.likelyCause: The glow ends on the hard, unlit cloud and surface silhouette taken from the half-resolution cloud geometry (nearest lookup, shaders/march.ts l.186) with no sub-pixel averaging from orbit (cloudJitter amplitude 0, src/render/atmosphere/clouds.ts l.640-644); the lowest 12 km of the limb, where the red is, is hidden by the dark cloud shell.
findings.fixDirection: March the limb band at full resolution (the criterion proposed for the Moon-distance view) or anti-alias the cloud silhouette in the composite; check the red layer against a cloud-free limb and against photographs.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/atmosphere/perf-60-000-km-1440p.png, perf-low-orbit-1440p.png and the six other perf-*-1440p.png; earth-moon-distance.png, ascent-25km.png, sampling-ascent-5km-horizon.png
findings.defect: Evidence hygiene. The eight perf-*-1440p.png frames (written 23:10-23:12 on 2026-11-10) predate the last commit to the package (401bd5e, 23:22:37) and still show the dot lattice in thin cloud that the commit addressed; they are the only native-1440p animated frames of the package. I re-ran the functional specs through the gate (45 passed, 1 skipped, 3.7 min): 72 screenshots were rewritten and the 'deterministic' captures are not reproducible between two runs of the same commit (pixels differing by more than 12/255: earth-moon-distance 5,227, ascent-25km 2,631, sampling-ascent-5km-horizon 2,015, tunables-coarse-steps 1,014). The 237 files in explore/ are tuning output from 17:00-23:18 and all but four predate the last three commits.
findings.realReference: A package judged by its pictures needs pictures of its current state that repeat exactly, at the resolution and in the mode the player sees.
findings.likelyCause: The perf spec is the only one that captures at 1440p in animated mode and was not re-run after the last change; the captures depend on temporal state at the moment of the screenshot (cloud history weight 0.125 after a fixed frame count, exposure adaptation, the cloud clock advanced by real frame time in advanceCloudClock).
findings.fixDirection: Add native-1440p animated captures of the acceptance views to the functional suite, reset cloud history and the cloud clock at scene set-up and wait for convergence before each screenshot, and delete or archive the stale explore/ and perf frames when the package changes.
